ABOUT SWEILLEM
# Ninety years of vitrified clay
“Daring to be the first, working hard for a world-class level” has been SWEILLEM’s philosophy since it began in Cairo in 1935.
## Who we are
In the heart of Cairo, Egypt, SWEILLEM started out in 1935 with a small plant manufacturing vitrified clay pipes. Learning, developing and keeping the same excellence of quality pushed SWEILLEM to serve and add to the vitrified clay pipe industry.
In 1987 SWEILLEM built a new factory with advanced production lines to meet the demands of the local market. Since then it has kept up with what is new in the field and expanded worldwide.
With full R&D facilities and an efficient technical team, SWEILLEM serves Egypt, the Middle East, the Far East and Europe. Warehouses in different parts of the world keep delivery times short, and the aim stays the same: continuous improvement in delivery time, price and performance.

title: How vitrified clay pipes are made
text:
MANUFACTURING PROCESS
# Six steps from Aswan clay to a finished joint
Every SWEILLEM pipe is moulded, dried, glazed inside and out, and fired at up to 1200 °C. Scroll to move one pipe through the factory, at your own pace.
## From Aswan clay to the trench
-
Step 01
### Raw material
The clay begins its journey at the quarry in Aswan. At the factory it is inspected and carefully stored.
-
Step 02
### Quality control
The clay is tested for its percentage of fine minerals, salts and aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃).
-
Step 03
### Moulding
Wet clay is kept in the right atmosphere until it reaches the extruders that shape each pipe. Specialised handling equipment carries it on to the dryers.
-
Step 04
### Drying
The pipe loses most of the water it needed for moulding. The dryers were built under the supervision of Lingl (Germany) and are fully computerised.
-
Step 05
### Glazing
After a quality check, each pipe is fully immersed in glaze, a thick liquid of natural materials, coating it inside and out.
-
Step 06
### Final firing
Pre-heating removes any remaining humidity. Shuttle kilns then fire each diameter on its own curve, up to 1200 °C over 2 to 4 days, turning the glaze into a glassy cover.
-
Step 07
### Joints
Factory-applied polyurethane joints seal each spigot in its socket. They stay watertight at 0.5, 1 and 2.4 bar, internal or external, and keep roots out.
-
Step 08
### Delivery
Finished pipes go directly from the factory, or from SWEILLEM's warehouses abroad, to projects in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Germany and beyond.
-
Step 09
### Installation
On site, each spigot is pushed into the next socket, forming a continuous, watertight sewer line underground.
## Each step, with the facts
-
STEP 01 OF 06
### Raw material
The clay begins its journey at the quarry in Aswan. On arrival at the factory it is inspected and carefully stored.
- Aswan clay
- Fine minerals checked
- Salts checked
- Al₂O₃ checked
-
STEP 02 OF 06
### Moulding
Wet clay is kept in the most suitable atmosphere until it reaches the extruders that mould each pipe. Specialised handling equipment carries the pipes on to the dryers in perfect condition.
- Extruders
- Specialised handling
-
STEP 03 OF 06
### Drying
The pipes lose most of the water that moulding needed. The dryers were built under the supervision of the German company Lingl, and their control is fully computerised.
- Lingl, Germany
- Computer controlled
-
STEP 04 OF 06
### Glazing
After drying and a quality check, each pipe is fully immersed in glaze, a thick liquid of natural materials. Firing turns it into a glassy cover inside and out, which keeps internal friction low and stops the inner surface absorbing.
- Full immersion
- Glazed inside and out
-
STEP 05 OF 06
### Firing
A pre-heating phase makes sure no humidity is left in the pipes. Shuttle kilns from a leading German American maker then fire each diameter on its own curve, up to a maximum of 1200 °C, over 2 to 4 days.
- Shuttle kilns
- Up to 1200 °C
- 2 to 4 days

STEP 06 OF 06
### Jointing
Spigot and socket are designed to seal watertight at 0.5, 1 and 2.4 bar, internal or external. A polyurethane joint of 67 ± 5 Shore A keeps roots out.

text:
QUALITY
# Made and tested to EN 295
SWEILLEM pipes are made to EN 295 in Normal (N) and High (H) strength classes, and to GSO EN 295 for the Gulf, from DN 125 to DN 1000.
## Strength classes by size
Every pipe size has a strength class (TKL) and a minimum crushing strength (FN, in kN per metre). H pipes are the extra-strength range.
SIZE DN | N pipes normal strength | H pipes extra strength
TKL | FN KN/M | TKL | FN KN/M

150 | - | 34 | - | -

250 | 160 | 40 | 240 | 60
300 | 160 | 48 | 240 | 72
350 | 160 | 56 | 200 | 70

600 | 95 | 57 | 160 | 96
700 | - | - | 120 | 84
800 | - | - | 120 | 96

1000 | - | - | 95 | 95
From the N and H pipe tables on sweillem.net, as published. “-” means the table gives no value for that size. Full dimensions are on the Pipes (/products/pipes) page.
## Standards SWEILLEM works to
Product standards for the pipes and their joints, and 3 certified management systems.
-
EN 295

-

Quality management

-
ISO 14001:2015
Environmental management

ISO 45001:2018
Health and safety management
Certificates 9720 and MSE 0640525C
See every certificate (/certificates)
## Where quality is checked
Checks named in SWEILLEM’s own description of how a pipe is made.
-
01
### Raw material
Aswan clay is inspected on arrival and tested for its share of fine minerals, salts and aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃).
-
02
### Before glazing
Dried pipes pass a quality check before they go to the glazing section.
-
03
### Firing
Shuttle kilns fire each diameter on its own curve up to 1200 °C, so the glaze becomes a glassy cover inside and out.
-
04
### Joints
Joints are tested for watertightness at 0.5, 1 and 2.4 bar and for angular deflection to EN 295-3:2012.
Joint performance (/joint-performance)
## Why vitrified clay lasts
PHYSICAL PROPERTIES
### Highest abrasion resistance
Vitrified clay is the most abrasion-resistant material for sewer lines. Its natural components handle sewage running at very high velocity through the line, up to 10 m/s.
CHEMICAL PROPERTIES
### Resistant to corrosion
Vitrified clay is the only sewer pipe material proven over centuries to resist sulfide-generated acids, most industrial wastes, solvents and aggressive soils. The H₂S formed when sulphur breaks down is what corrodes most sewer pipes. Resisting it gives vitrified clay pipes a life expectancy of more than 100 years.
From About Us on sweillem.net.

text:
NEW PRODUCT LINE
# Clay roof tiles
SWEILLEM’s second product line, made in Egypt. Roof tiles come in various designs, colours and profiles. Pick a colour to see it up close or across a roof.
COLOUR
Terracotta
Blue
Black
VIEW
Single tile
On a roof
Showing terracotta, photographed by SWEILLEM.
HOW A TILE IS MADE
## From the Aswan quarry to the roof
Scroll to follow a tile through nine steps. The explanation for each step sits under the picture.
-
Step 01
### Collecting the clay
The clay begins its journey from the quarry of Aswan, where it is dug and loaded for the trip to the factory.
-
Step 02
### Inspection and storage
On arrival the raw material is inspected and carefully stored. Quality checks cover the share of fine minerals, the share of salts and the aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) in the clay.
-
Step 03
### Moulding
The wet clay is kept in the right atmosphere until it is moulded into shape, then carried on to the dryers in perfect condition.
-
Step 04
### Drying
Drying takes out most of the water the moulding needed. The dryers were built under the supervision of the German company Lingl, and their control is fully computerised.
-
Step 05
### Colour and glaze
After quality control the dried clay gets its finish. SWEILLEM offers its tiles in terracotta, blue and black.
-
Step 06
### Firing
Shuttle kilns follow the best firing curve up to a maximum of 1200 degrees, over two to four days. The fire turns soft clay into hard ceramic.
-
Step 07
### Quality control and packing
Finished tiles are checked and stacked for dispatch. Every tile is stamped “Made in Egypt” and “SWEILLEM”.
-
Step 08
### Delivery
Efficiency, accuracy, delivery on time: the tiles travel from the factory to the building site.
-
Step 09
### On the roof
Row by row, from the eaves to the ridge, the tiles close the roof. This last scene is an illustration.
Steps from SWEILLEM’s published manufacturing process (About and the company deck), which SWEILLEM describes for its clay products. ## What each scope covers
SWEILLEM follows the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, which separates direct emissions from those in the supply chain.
-
DECLARED
### Scope 1
Direct emissions
Greenhouse gas from sources SWEILLEM owns or controls, such as fuel burned in vehicles and in facility processes. At SWEILLEM this is mainly the gas burned at the kilns.
-
DECLARED
### Scope 2
Indirect: electricity
Emissions from the electricity, steam, heat or cooling SWEILLEM buys, mainly for its offices and production facilities.
-
IN DEVELOPMENT
### Scope 3
Other indirect emissions
Emissions in the wider supply chain. SWEILLEM is still developing these calculations.
## Pipes made to last
CRADLE TO CRADLE CERTIFIED · BRONZE
### Certified for circularity
SWEILLEM’s vitrified clay pipes DN 125 to DN 1000 with accessories are Cradle to Cradle Certified at Full Scope Bronze level (version 4.1, certificate 9605, May 2025 to May 2028).
View the certificate (/certificates)
MORE THAN 100 YEARS
### A long service life
Vitrified clay resists corrosion from sewer gases, industrial wastes and aggressive soils, which gives the pipes a life expectancy of more than 100 years. SWEILLEM’s environmental management is certified to ISO 14001.
